slides.title: Why do your dog's eyes *glow* in photos?
There is a mirror in there.
slides.body: Behind the retina is a layer called the tapetum lucidum. It reflects light.

slides.title: It helps in low light.
slides.body: The mirror gives the eye a second chance to catch light. Dogs evolved to hunt in the dark.

slides.title: That is your glow.
slides.body: The flash bounces back out. It can look green, blue, orange or yellow.

slides.title: Knowing dogs is our *job.*
slides.body: Tell us how your dog moves, plays and rests. We will plan their stay.

posts.caption:
Ever notice your dog's eyes glow in a flash photo?

Behind the retina is a layer called the tapetum lucidum. It works like a mirror. It bounces light back so the eye gets a second chance to catch it. That helps dogs see in low light.

The glow you see is that light coming back out. It can look green, blue, orange or yellow.

Save this for the next time you take a photo at night.
